svg.title: What an Invoice Turns Into on Day One
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-factoring-invoice-funnel; chapter number: 6; chart type: funnel; title: What an Invoice Turns Into on Day One; subtitle: Advance and discount levels as a percent of invoice face value; caption: A B2B invoice for delivered work is sold to a factor, which advances most of the face value immediately and charges a discount per batch.; assumptions note: All values are percent of invoice face value. Advance levels come from Joe Camberato and Ian Johnson; discount levels come from CPA Financial Exchange Group and are quoted per batch, never annualized.; note: Sources are Joe Camberato, Ian Johnson, CPA Financial Exchange Group, and Universal Funding Corporation.; stages: label: Invoice face value; value: 100; display: 100% of invoice; conversion: Invoice sent to the customer and to the factor; detail: Underwriting rests on the account debtor's credit rating, not the client's, per Ian Johnson.; label: Day-one advance ceiling; value: 90; display: Up to 90%; conversion: Paid immediately on invoicing; detail: Camberato quotes advances of 80 to 90 percent on day one.; label: Modeled advance; value: 80; display: 80%; conversion: Johnson's worksheet advance; detail: Johnson models an 80 percent advance plus a typical 1 percent administration fee.; label: Industry-average discount ceiling; value: 4.5; display: Up to 4.5% per batch; conversion: Industry average 3% to 4.5%; detail: Per batch of receivables purchased, not annualized.; label: Typical first-30-day discount; value: 3; display: 3% first 30 days; conversion: Plus 1% for each additional period; detail: Referral brokers earn 20 percent for the life of the deal through Universal Funding Corporation.

text.title: What an Invoice Turns Into on Day One
text.tspan: What an Invoice Turns Into on Day One

rect.title: label: Invoice face value; value: 100; display: 100% of invoice; conversion: Invoice sent to the customer and to the factor; detail: Underwriting rests on the account debtor's credit rating, not the client's, per Ian Johnson.
label: Day-one advance ceiling; value: 90; display: Up to 90%; conversion: Paid immediately on invoicing; detail: Camberato quotes advances of 80 to 90 percent on day one.
label: Modeled advance; value: 80; display: 80%; conversion: Johnson's worksheet advance; detail: Johnson models an 80 percent advance plus a typical 1 percent administration fee.
label: Industry-average discount ceiling; value: 4.5; display: Up to 4.5% per batch; conversion: Industry average 3% to 4.5%; detail: Per batch of receivables purchased, not annualized.

label: Typical first-30-day discount; value: 3; display: 3% first 30 days; conversion: Plus 1% for each additional period; detail: Referral brokers earn 20 percent for the life of the deal through Universal Funding Corporation.

text.title: Assumptions: All values are percent of invoice face value. Advance levels come from Joe Camberato and Ian Johnson; discount levels come from CPA Financial Exchange Group and are quoted per batch, never annualized.
text.tspan: Assumptions: All values are percent of invoice face value. Advance levels come from Joe Camberato and Ian Johnson; discount levels
come from CPA Financial Exchange Group and are quoted per batch, never annualized.
